Check Whether Age Groups Can Be Aggregated to a Target Classification

Source: R/age_diagnose_coarsen.R
age_diagnose_coarsen.Rd

Check that observations labelled by labels can be aggregated to the age groups in to, without splitting observations, omitting required ages, or counting ages more than once.

age_diagnose_coarsen() reports the results of the checks. age_assert_coarsen() returns labels invisibly if the checks pass, and throws an error otherwise. Neither function recodes the labels or aggregates observations.

Usage

age_diagnose_coarsen(
  labels,
  to,
  include_equals = TRUE,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent"),
  x_arg = rlang::caller_arg(labels),
  to_arg = rlang::caller_arg(to)
)

age_assert_coarsen(
  labels,
  to,
  include_equals = TRUE,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent"),
  x_arg = rlang::caller_arg(labels),
  to_arg = rlang::caller_arg(to),
  call = rlang::current_env()
)

Arguments

labels

Vector of age group labels.

to

Vector of age group labels giving the target classification.

include_equals

Whether to allow identical classifications. Default is TRUE. Set to FALSE to require at least one genuine merge.

interpret_fail

Action if a label cannot be interpreted: "error" (the default), "warn", or "silent". Uninterpretable labels fail the checks even when parsing errors are suppressed.

x_arg

Name of labels to use in error and warning messages. Defaults to the expression supplied for labels.

to_arg

Name of to to use in error and warning messages. Defaults to the expression supplied for to.

call

Execution environment of the function to name in errors from age_assert_coarsen(). Defaults to the assertion itself. A calling function can supply call = rlang::current_env().

Value

  • age_diagnose_coarsen() returns a list with a logical flag ok and a tibble details, with columns condition, passed, and comment, as in age_diagnose_values(). Checks that depend on earlier failed checks are omitted. Comments give an example of each failure.

  • age_assert_coarsen() returns the original labels invisibly, or raises an error explaining the failures.

Two empty inputs pass when include_equals = TRUE. An empty input paired with a nonempty input fails.

Details

Both inputs must consist of age intervals, with no totals, missing categories, or NA values. Within each input, intervals must not overlap. Repeated labels, and different labels describing the same interval, count as overlapping.

Every source interval must fit wholly inside exactly one target interval. The source intervals assigned to each target must cover it completely, with no gaps. The classifications may have gaps between target intervals, provided that the source has the same gaps. Use age_assert_values() with no_gap = TRUE if continuous coverage is also required.

By default, identical classifications pass. Equality is based on intervals, regardless of spelling or ordering. With include_equals = FALSE, at least one target interval must combine two or more source intervals; other intervals may stay unchanged.

Unlike age_coarsen_to(), these functions also check for overlaps among source observations and for complete coverage of every target. They do not check the values being aggregated, or whether other join keys such as country and year match between datasets.

Factors

Both functions check the observed values of labels and to. Unused factor levels are ignored, as in age_assert_values(). To check a classification defined by all factor levels instead, supply levels(x) explicitly.

age_coarsen_to() uses all factor levels when recoding. To coarsen only the values checked here, supply droplevels(labels) and droplevels(to) when the inputs are factors, or convert them to character vectors.

See also

  • age_coarsen_to(), age_mapping(), age_assert_values()

  • period_assert_coarsen(), period_diagnose_coarsen()

  • cohort_assert_coarsen(), cohort_diagnose_coarsen()

Examples

age <- c("0-4", "5-9", "10+")
target <- c("0-9", "10+")
age_assert_coarsen(age, to = target)
age_coarsen_to(age, to = target)
#> [1] 0-9 0-9 10+
#> Levels: 0-9 10+

## equality is allowed by default
age_assert_coarsen(target, to = target)
age_diagnose_coarsen(target, to = target, include_equals = FALSE)
#> $ok
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $details
#> # A tibble: 7 × 3
#>   condition         passed comment                                              
#>   <chr>             <lgl>  <chr>                                                
#> 1 labels_intervals  TRUE   NA                                                   
#> 2 to_intervals      TRUE   NA                                                   
#> 3 labels_no_overlap TRUE   NA                                                   
#> 4 to_no_overlap     TRUE   NA                                                   
#> 5 contained         TRUE   NA                                                   
#> 6 complete          TRUE   NA                                                   
#> 7 not_equal         FALSE  Source and target describe the same classification; …
#> 

## target 0-9 is missing source ages 5-9
age_diagnose_coarsen(c("0-4", "10+"), to = target)
#> $ok
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $details
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   condition         passed comment                                              
#>   <chr>             <lgl>  <chr>                                                
#> 1 labels_intervals  TRUE    NA                                                  
#> 2 to_intervals      TRUE    NA                                                  
#> 3 labels_no_overlap TRUE    NA                                                  
#> 4 to_no_overlap     TRUE    NA                                                  
#> 5 contained         TRUE    NA                                                  
#> 6 complete          FALSE  "Target '0-9' in 'target' is not fully covered; sour…
#> 

## a source interval crosses a target boundary
age_diagnose_coarsen(c("0-6", "7+"), to = target)
#> $ok
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $details
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>   condition         passed comment                                              
#>   <chr>             <lgl>  <chr>                                                
#> 1 labels_intervals  TRUE    NA                                                  
#> 2 to_intervals      TRUE    NA                                                  
#> 3 labels_no_overlap TRUE    NA                                                  
#> 4 to_no_overlap     TRUE    NA                                                  
#> 5 contained         FALSE  "Source '7+' in 'c(\"0-6\", \"7+\")' does not fit wh…
#> 

## matching gaps between targets are allowed
age_assert_coarsen(c("0-4", "5-9", "20+"), to = c("0-9", "20+"))

## check and aggregate separately within groups
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
df <- data.frame(
  sex = rep(c("Female", "Male"), each = 3),
  age = rep(age, 2),
  deaths = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
)
df |>
  mutate(age = age_assert_coarsen(age, to = target), .by = sex) |>
  mutate(age = age_coarsen_to(age, to = target), .by = sex) |>
  summarise(deaths = sum(deaths), .by = c(sex, age))
#>      sex age deaths
#> 1 Female 0-9      3
#> 2 Female 10+      3
#> 3   Male 0-9      9
#> 4   Male 10+      6
